name: @insolvia-ai/app
//: The Insolvia app — Expo / React Native, shipped as a web SPA.
A member of the root npm workspace, so `npm ci` at the repo root installs
it and symlinks @insolvia-ai/tokens. There is NO component library and NO
styling library here: bare React Native primitives + StyleSheet.create,
settled by measurement (docs/adr/0004). Adding gluestack, NativeWind,
Unistyles or Tailwind is a regression, not an upgrade.
Expo's FREE tier only: none of the paid EAS services, no EAS config file,
no EAS command-line tool, no Expo access token in CI, and no over-the-air
updates package. Web builds run in GitHub Actions and hosting is the
existing S3 + CloudFront (infra/modules/web_hosting). A CI step greps for
those names, which is why they are described here rather than spelled out.
ios/ and android/ are deliberately absent: `expo prebuild` generates them
//scripts: .github/workflows/app-*.yml — renaming one orphans a required check.
http://localhost:3000 as an EXACT-MATCH Cognito allowed origin; Expo's own
default is 8081, which that origin list would reject.
`build` passes --clear: Metro's transform cache keys on file content and
config, NOT on environment variables, so a staging export followed by a
production export in the same job can otherwise reuse the staging bundle
and ship it as production (EXPO_PUBLIC_INSOLVIA_ENV is inlined at
transform time). The cost is a cold Metro cache per build; the failure it
prevents is shipping the wrong API base URL.
//dependencies: Versions are verified end-to-end as a set and pinned as one: Expo SDK
with `npx expo install --check`, never one package at a time.
/v1/me), built with the accessToken provider seam that src/session hands it.
Sign-in adds NO dependency: PKCE is Web Crypto and storage is the platform
localStorage/sessionStorage, each read lazily behind a guard in
async-storage are deliberately absent — a future NATIVE client (custom-scheme
redirect, system browser, platform secure store) is what would justify the
first of them; on web it would buy nothing. See docs/adr/0007.
//insolvia-ai-dependencies: from github.com/insolvia-ai/design-system, pinned by range like any other
dependency. They were `*` while they were workspace members of this repo,
which meant this app read the design system's SOURCE through a symlink and
saw every merge instantly — while the marketing site, installing the
published version, saw nothing until a release. Extracting them ended that
split. Take a change by bumping the range here, never by pointing it at a
@insolvia-ai/api-client stays `*`: it IS still a workspace member of this
repo, and the symlink is correct for it.
//react-test-renderer: A peer of @testing-library/react-native, pinned to the SAME version as
react. It must be declared: left to npm, the peer resolves to the newest
react-test-renderer, whose own `react` peer is then narrower than our
pinned 19.2.3 and the install fails with ERESOLVE. Bump it in lockstep with
//jest: The config moved to jest.config.js — it has to COMPUTE
`transformIgnorePatterns` from jest-expo's own, which package.json cannot
do. @insolvia-ai/design-system publishes untranspiled source and now lives
under node_modules (it was a workspace member before the extraction), so
Jest skips transforming it and every route test dies on `export`. That
file explains why the list is derived rather than pasted; the preset's own
Tests assert accessibility PROPS (role, aria-level, aria-labelledby); that
those props become real <h1>/<button>/<label>-equivalent tags is
react-native-web's own mapping, re-verified against the built DOM in the
deploy checks rather than mocked here.
